messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for cluster us-west-2 — llama-mqa-prod. Symptom: KV cache size growth + continuous-batch queue depth spike. Error rate up 6.2% 5xx in the last 3m. Auto-runbook: collect heap+kv-stats and notify oncall.

oncall-lucas: on it. pulling logs and current configs. tagging matt + asha.

matt (eng-runtime): seeing a rapid climb in `kv.prefix_shard_size` for model variant llama-mqa-v3; continuous batch growth correlates with prefetch worker logs that show repeated prefix miss storms. suspect migratory prefixes causing bubbles that keep re-populating the cache.

julia (sre): is this isolated to us-west-2 or cross-region? any customer-facing 429/timeout alerts?

asha (ml-infra): initial check: only us-west-2 hosts show the 10x prefix blowup. prefetch queue shows many parallel fetches for long (>2s) keys. looks like prefetch + continuous batching are interacting: batches are coalescing with stale KV entries and then triggering re-prefetch.

sam (customer-svcs): receiving inbound tickets: 3 production customers reporting slow responses and increased latencies. one enterprise customer (org: BrightLane) hit their 99p SLA. CC: sales-eng on the call.

matt (eng-runtime): mitigation plan proposal: 1) throttle continuous batching to reduce in-flight growth; 2) disable prefetch for llama-mqa briefly; 3) force targeted eviction for top offending prefix shards; 4) monitor error-rate and re-enable gradually.

julia (sre): agree. do we have an immediate hotfix command? want to avoid full restart.

matt (eng-runtime): we can flip feature flags and use rolling restarts for prefetch workers only. commands:

```bash
# throttle continuous batching globally for llama-mqa
rwdctl config set --service llama-mqa --key batching.continuous.max_inflight --value 1
# disable prefetch queue processors for the modelvariant
rwdctl feature-flag set --ff prefetch.llama-mqa.enabled false
# targeted eviction (prefix shards from logs)
rwdctl cache evict --cluster us-west-2 --model llama-mqa --prefix-shard shard-42,shard-47
```

oncall-lucas: applying throttle now. running first command.

devops-bot: executed: rwdctl config set --service llama-mqa --key batching.continuous.max_inflight --value 1 (ok)

matt (eng-runtime): flipping prefetch next. doing a rolling stop of prefetch workers only to avoid inference disruption.

devops-bot: feature-flag change applied: prefetch.llama-mqa.enabled=false (ok). rolling prefetch-worker pool restart initiated.

asha (ml-infra): starting targeted eviction for shards reported in logs. evicting shard-42 and shard-47.

devops-bot: cache evict job started (job-id: evict-1988-01).

julia (sre): watch dashboards please: token-per-request, kv-shard-size, continuous-batch-depth, 5xx-rate. set alert on any regression.

matt (eng-runtime): quick log snippet after eviction:
```
[2026-03-15T02:17:10Z] INFO kv: evicted shard-42 keys=124k freed=1.9GB
[2026-03-15T02:17:13Z] INFO prefetch: worker-stopped id=59
[2026-03-15T02:17:20Z] WARN batching: inflight reduced to 1 for llama-mqa
```

oncall-lucas: 5xx rate trending down. 99p latency for BrightLane improving from 9.3s to 1.8s within 6m.

sam (customer-svcs): notified BrightLane (initial mitigation + ETA for full recovery). they asked for a timeline — told them < 30m to stable.

julia (sre): good. can we confirm root cause quick: is it a model change or config drift?

asha (ml-infra): correlating with recent rollout: a model-serving change was deployed yesterday which enabled more aggressive prefetch heuristics for MQA (prefetch.hot_prefix_threshold lowered). combined with a spike in user prompt prefixes for a small set of customers, this produced a migratory prefix hot-set that tortured the cache. so root cause: heuristic+traffic pattern interaction.

matt (eng-runtime): TL;DR: prefetch heuristic too eager + continuous batching handshake amplified the cache churn.

oncall-lucas: handoff: i'll be on pager for 90m to verify stable. julia will take postmortem lead and asha will own infra/heuristic rollback. sam will coordinate customer comms and collect impacted org list.

julia (sre): postmortem action items (quick):
- rollback prefetch heuristic change for MQA (owner: asha, due: 24h)
- add guardrail to prefetch to limit per-prefix concurrency (owner: matt, due: 72h)
- improve alerting to detect prefix-migration patterns earlier (owner: julia, due: 48h)
- run chaos test for prefetch + continuous-batching interaction (owner: eng-runtime, due: 7d)

sam (customer-svcs): logged impacted customers: BrightLane, Nuvita, FlowAI. will prepare templated outreach and coordinate crediting.

matt (eng-runtime): also adding a temporary telemetry tag so we can track any re-introduced prefix storms if we re-enable prefetch.

oncall-lucas: current status: stable, 5xx below baseline, evictions reduced shard sizes. keeping pager open until 04:00 UTC. will escalate to full incident if any regression.

julia (sre): note for postmortem: include timeline of heuristic rollout, config diffs, and the early-warning thresholds. will schedule P0 postmortem meeting and invite infra + runtime + product.

sam (customer-svcs): sending update to impacted customers now.

matt (eng-runtime): thanks everyone. will follow up with logs and commands run in the incident doc.

IncidentBot: Incident marked as mitigated at 02:46 UTC. Pager status: watching.

julia (sre): handing off to oncall-lucas. tagging this thread for postmortem prep.

oncall-lucas: acknowledged. staying on watch.
